title: Emergency Capacity Telemetry Snapshot — May 22 2026
summary: Ad-hoc telemetry extraction to support postmortem for May 22 capacity incident. Pull covers GPU queueing, throttle events, batching efficiency, prefix cache hit rates, and regional throttles across prod clusters between 2026-05-22T00:00:00Z and 2026-05-22T06:00:00Z.
content:
Purpose:
- Produce a compact, queryable snapshot of telemetry to accelerate root-cause analysis for the 2026-05-22 capacity incident.
- Focus on signals that correlate with user-facing throttles and latency SLO violations: GPU queue length, throttle events (reason/tag), batching efficiency, KV cache hit rate, model variant fallback, and regional request distributions.

Scope & time windows:
- Primary window: 2026-05-22T00:00:00Z -> 2026-05-22T06:00:00Z (6h)
- Extended window for baseline comparison: 2026-05-15T00:00:00Z -> 2026-05-22T00:00:00Z (7d)
- Granularity: 1m and 5m aggregates where applicable.

Columns for exported CSV / sheet (ordering used in the extraction):
- sample_ts (ISO8601)
- region
- cloud_zone
- cluster_id
- node_pool
- instance_id
- gpu_type
- model_family
- model_version
- endpoint_id
- route_id
- request_type (text/generate/emb/stream)
- tokens_in
- tokens_out
- queue_length (int)
- concurrent_requests (int)
- active_gpu_streams (int)
- batching_efficiency (float 0-1)
- avg_latency_ms
- p95_latency_ms
- throttle_event_count
- throttle_reason (one of: capacity, policy, model_timeout, region_quota)
- throttle_rate (0-1 fraction of requests throttled)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (0-1)
- gpu_util_pct (0-100)
- gpu_mem_util_pct (0-100)
- cpu_util_pct
- prefix_cache_miss_spike (bool)
- fallback_model_id (nullable)
- rollout_tag
- request_id_sample (for quick trace lookups)

Primary BigQuery extraction (examples to run in bq console):
- -- 1m aggregation with relevant joins (telemetry, throttles, model_routes)
- SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_ts, MINUTE) AS sample_ts,
  region,
  cluster_id,
  ANY_VALUE(gpu_type) AS gpu_type,
  SUM(queue_len) AS queue_length,
  AVG(batching_eff) AS batching_efficiency,
  SUM(throttle_count) AS throttle_event_count,
  APPROX_TOP_N(throttle_reason,1)[OFFSET(0)].value AS throttle_reason,
  AVG(p95_latency_ms) AS p95_latency_ms,
  AVG(kv_cache_hit_rate) AS kv_cache_hit_rate
  FROM `redwood-prod.telemetry.inference_events`
  WHERE event_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-05-22T00:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-05-22T06:00:00Z')
  GROUP BY sample_ts, region, cluster_id
  ORDER BY sample_ts;

- Note: above is a template — use project-specific dataset names and join with throttles table to pull per-route reason and request ids. Keep queries limited to ~1h windows in interactive runs to avoid BigQuery slot/scan cost.

Quick anomalies observed from the extracted snapshot (preliminary):
- Two clusters in us-east1 (cluster-c-7 and cluster-c-9) show persistent queue_length > 4x baseline between 02:10 and 03:05 UTC. Correlated with a spike in prefix_cache_miss (from ~8% baseline to ~62%).
- Throttle events labeled 'capacity' and 'region_quota' increased sharply in us-east1 and eu-west1 during the window. Throttle_rate peaked at ~0.28 in us-east1 02:17 UTC.
- Batching efficiency dropped from 0.78 to 0.41 on impacted nodes, coincident with a model rollout_tag (canary-v2) rolling from 01:50 -> 02:05 in the same clusters. Several requests fell back to fallback_model_id=v1-quant leading to increased token counts and longer generation times.
- GPU util stayed high (~92%) but GPU memory utilization did not change proportionally, suggesting compute-bound work (longer sequences / more attention overhead) rather than out-of-memory.

Sampling & drill plan (how to use this sheet during postmortem):
- Pivot by region -> cluster -> minute to identify exact minute of onset.
- Filter rows where throttle_event_count > 0 and sample_ts within +/- 10 minutes of throttle spikes. Pull request_id_sample and run traces in tracing UI.
- Compare batching_efficiency and kv_cache_hit_rate with deploy timeline using rollout_tag to see causal relationship with canary.
- Cross-check traffic funnels (per-route RPS) to identify if a single tenant or route caused increased long-token requests.

Minimal reproducible queries for on-call/SEs (short snippets):
- Find top 10 routes by throttle_rate in window: SELECT route_id, SUM(throttle_count)/SUM(requests) AS throttle_rate FROM telemetry.throttles WHERE ts BETWEEN ... GROUP BY route_id ORDER BY throttle_rate DESC LIMIT 10;
- Correlate kv_cache misses with queueing: SELECT sample_ts, region, AVG(queue_length) AS qlen, AVG(kv_cache_hit_rate) AS hit FROM telemetry.aggregates WHERE sample_ts BETWEEN ... GROUP BY sample_ts, region ORDER BY sample_ts;

Counts & cardinality notes (from a representative extract):
- total rows (6h, 1m granularity): ~34,800 rows
- distinct clusters observed: 24
- distinct routes in window: ~184
- throttle_event rows: 1,142 entries (peak density us-east1/us-west2)

Preliminary root-cause hypothesis (working):
- Canary rollout of a larger-context canary model (canary-v2) increased average tokens_out per request and reduced batching efficiency for certain request patterns. This caused more compute per request, leading to sustained GPU queueing on a subset of clusters. Simultaneous prefix cache miss spike magnified per-request token processing and prevented quick KV cache reuse. Throttles were applied at regional capacity and quota layers, causing visible user impacts.

Immediate mitigation actions taken (and by whom):
- 02:25 UTC: roll back rollout_tag canary-v2 -> rollback to stable v1 (owner: Mei Huang).
- 02:40 UTC: temporarily increase burst capacity in us-east1 by enabling reserved_pools (owner: Riley Thompson).
- 03:10 UTC: re-enable prefix cache warmers for high-traffic routes to restore hit rates (owner: Diego Alvarez).

Open follow-ups / next steps (owners & target dates):
- Quantify cost vs. user impact of enabling larger-context models in canary: owner Jordan Kim, due 2026-05-29.
- Add automations to block canary rollouts that increase expected tokens_out > 30% without pre-approval: owner platform-engineering, due 2026-06-12.
- Add an alert for cross-metric anomaly where batching_efficiency drops > 30% and kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.5 for > 10m: owner SRE, due 2026-06-05.
- Add a dashboard tile showing per-rollout expected token_delta and predicted GPU impact (model rollout tool integration): owner product-hosted-api, due 2026-06-19.

Notes about data quality & caveats:
- Telemetry is sampled at node level and some high-cardinality fields (request_id_sample) are approximate due to sampling. For exact tracing use the trace IDs from the tracing system.
- BigQuery schema evolved on 2026-04-11 (added batching_efficiency) — older baselines should be adjusted accordingly.
- Some Grafana panels truncate legends; use direct query links from linked_artifacts for full context.

Attachments included with this sheet:
- CSV extract: emergency_capacity_snapshot_2026-05-22.csv (GCS link in linked_artifacts)
- Top 50 request trace ids for peak minutes: trace-ids-2026-05-22-peak.txt

How to reproduce the extraction locally (runbook):
1) Open BigQuery console and select redwood-prod project.
2) Copy main query template (section above) and set time bounds. Use 1m groupings and LIMIT 20000 per run for interactive.
3) Export to GCS as CSV and attach to the incident ticket.
4) Load into this sheet for pivoting and annotation.

Contact for clarifications: Jordan Kim (jordan.kim@redwood.com) — available on #incident-capacity and /pager for follow-ups.
